module.api_endpoints.checks: Probes API and tooling paths (OpenAPI/Swagger, Spring Actuator, Prometheus, GraphQL, Elasticsearch, Vault…) and keeps an endpoint only if its content has the expected shape; GraphQL introspection is confirmed with a dedicated request.
module.api_endpoints.fix:
Remove the exposure without waiting: block public access to the flagged paths (documentation `/swagger-ui.html`, `/openapi.json`, `/v3/api-docs`, console `/actuator`, metrics `/metrics`, administration tools) with a reverse proxy or firewall rule that lets through only your internal network, your VPN or your IP addresses (nginx snippet).
If `/actuator/env`, `/actuator/heapdump`, a debug console or an API exposed environment variables, passwords, keys or tokens: treat them as compromised, renew them, then review the access logs for unknown requests.
Spring Boot Actuator: expose only `health` (`management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health`), move management to an internal port (`management.server.port` and `management.server.address=127.0.0.1`) and protect the rest with Spring Security (Spring Boot snippet).
OpenAPI or Swagger documentation: disable it in production (`springdoc.api-docs.enabled=false` for Spring, `docs_url=None` and `openapi_url=None` for FastAPI) or put it behind authentication. Public documentation is acceptable only for a deliberately open API.
GraphQL: disable introspection in production (`introspection: false` with Apollo Server, or the equivalent setting of your server), limit query depth and cost, and require authentication for non-public data.
Prometheus metrics and side tools (Telescope, Horizon, Elasticsearch, Vault, Grafana): never publish them on the Internet; make them listen on the internal network, behind a VPN or an authentication proxy.
For a truly public API: require authentication for any non-public data, limit the request rate and return plain errors, without stack traces.
Check: from an unauthorized network, `curl -sI https://example.com/actuator` and `curl -sI https://example.com/v3/api-docs` must return `403` or `404`; then run the scan again.
module.api_endpoints.title: API and development endpoints
module.api_endpoints.why: Public API documentation, an Actuator console or GraphQL introspection expose internal structure and sometimes sensitive data, making it easier to find flaws.
